newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to meet top legislator in Kremlin Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to meet top legislator in Kremlin Thursday.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, observing a light work schedule as he recovers from pneumonia, will return to the Kremlin on Thursday to meet the head of the upper house of parliament, his press office said.
A spokesman said Yeltsin would meet Federation Council Chairman Yegor Stroyev on his fifth visit to the Kremlin since leaving hospital on January 20.
Yeltsin, 66, fell ill with pneumonia exactly a month ago, and now spends most of his time recovering in an official residence outside Moscow. In November, he had quintuple heart bypass surgery.
His last visit to the Kremlin was on Tuesday when he met Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.

Television film of this and other recent meetings have shown a Yeltsin who has aged since he was taken ill with heart problems and then pneumonia. Aides say he is anxious to return to work but doctors counsel against haste.
The Kremlin did not say what Yeltsin would be discussing with Stroyev, a former communist who has largely been loyal to Yeltsin since assuming the Federation Council's top position.
But recently Stroyev said that the Russian constitution -- which gives the president overwhelming powers -- should be changed to give the parliament more influence.

Russia's current constitution was approved by a popular vote after Yeltsin disbanded the former parliament using military force in 1993. It would be extremely difficult to change under the rules for its amendment.
"I think the time is here when we have to take a harder critical look at the current constitution," Stroyev said last month. "The country can no longer live by (presidential) decree."

Because Yeltsin's illnesses have kept him from work for most of the time since his re-election in July last year, a growing number of Russians have called for constitutional changes to make the country less dependent on the rule of the president.
Yeltsin and Stroyev have kept in touch in recent months despite Yeltsin's prolonged illnesses. Stroyev went to Yeltsin's country house near Moscow in the autumn to see him prior to his heart surgery.
Stroyev was expected to brief reporters on his latest meeting later on Thursday.
